h1: Ao Kao White Sand Beach Resort — villas on Ao Kao Beach with a private roof terrace for stargazing
intro: If you want a Koh Mak stay that feels fresher than the usual wooden bungalow, Ao Kao White Sand Beach Resort delivers — the old bungalows were rebuilt as modern brushed-concrete villas, each with a private roof terrace and loungers under a thatched awning, perfect for an evening drink or stargazing. It sits on the eastern end of Ao Kao Beach next to Lazy Day, with an outdoor pool, a seaview rooftop bar and a beachfront restaurant. From approx. ฿1,500/night. Rated around 9.1 from real guest reviews.

body.html: Ao Kao White Sand is one of the resorts on Ao Kao Beach that has clearly reinvented itself — the old wooden bungalows have been replaced with modern brushed-concrete villas that look cleaner and more contemporary than much of what you'll find on the island. What guests mention most is that every villa has a private roof terrace with loungers under a thatched awning — a great spot for an evening drink or stargazing at night, the kind of feature you rarely get at this price point.

The resort sits at the eastern end of Ao Kao Beach, right next to Lazy Day The Resort. Ao Kao is a long beach on the southern side of the island, with white sand and rows of coconut palms. Out front there's an outdoor pool in the garden, a rooftop bar looking out to sea, and a beachfront restaurant where guests say the breakfast view is lovely. Kayaks, SUP boards and mountain bikes are available to rent, and there's a tennis court and a dive centre — plenty for anyone who wants to be active or paddle around the island.
"The villa was clean, spacious and stylish, with a private roof terrace we used all day. The staff were so warm and helpful, the beach out front was quiet, and the sunsets were beautiful."

There are two main villa categories. The garden-view villas are laid out in rows either side of a lawn and footpath, some set around the central pool, at the more affordable end. The beachfront villas sit right in front of the sand for roughly ฿1,000 more. Each villa is around 40 sqm with air conditioning, TV, mini-bar, fridge, drinking water, an en-suite bathroom and the roof terrace above. Many reviews praise the rooms as spacious and clean with well-kept furnishings, though some villas are starting to show their age.

Honestly, from the reviews: the point that comes up most is that the beach in front of the resort is fairly shallow at low tide with some rocky patches, so walking into deeper water isn't easy at every hour. At times there's plastic washed up on the adjacent public beach (an island-wide issue, not just here). Wi-Fi is weak in spots, and there aren't many dinner options within walking distance — you'll want to rent transport or walk about 10 minutes to the cluster of restaurants in the middle of the beach.

What guests consistently praise is warm, attentive staff — the staff score is especially high across platforms. There are small touches like a welcome plate of tropical fruit, easy scooter and golf-cart rentals, and a seaview rooftop bar that's a relaxed place to sit in the evening. It suits couples, groups of friends and families who want a good-looking villa at a price that's still reasonable — not chasing luxury, but offering a calm slice of Koh Mak with contemporary design.

The bottom line from real reviews: Ao Kao White Sand is a sensible pick for anyone who wants a modern villa with a private roof terrace on Ao Kao Beach. From around ฿1,500/night in normal season for a garden-view villa, rising in high season and for beachfront villas to roughly ฿3,600–5,200. It scores around 9.1 from real guests. If you can accept a beach that's shallow at low tide and dinner options that take a short ride, the design, service and beachfront location here are good value on Koh Mak.

honestSummary: Ao Kao White Sand is a resort that sells modern villa design and warm service — brushed-concrete villas with private roof terraces on Ao Kao Beach, a pool, and a seaview rooftop bar, great for couples and families. The trade-off is a beach that's shallow and rocky at low tide and dinners that take a short ride; if you can accept that, the design and service here are good value on Koh Mak.
honestChecks: If a beautiful, deep-water beach you can swim in any time is your priority — the shore here is shallow with some rocks at low tide → time it with high tide, or use the resort pool when the tide is out.
If you need reliable Wi-Fi to work — the signal is weak in places → ask for a villa near the main building/lobby and bring a backup mobile data SIM.
If you're going in low season (Jun–mid-Oct) — many places on Koh Mak close and the sea can be rough on some days → confirm with the resort that it's open and that boats are running before you book.

tips.title: Ask for a beachfront villa for the view
tips.body: Beachfront villas cost roughly ฿1,000 more but give you a full sunset view from your private roof terrace — worth it for a special trip.

tips.title: Check the tide times
tips.body: The beach in front gets shallow and rocky at low tide. If you want to swim in deeper water, check the tide chart, or use the resort pool instead.

tips.title: Rent transport for dinner
tips.body: There aren't many dinner spots within walking distance. Rent a scooter or golf cart at the resort to reach the restaurant cluster in the middle of the beach.

tips.title: Bring your own mosquito repellent
tips.body: Koh Mak is a natural island and there are mosquitoes in the gardens at dusk. Pack repellent and keep the room closed with the AC on in the evening.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Ao Kao White Sand Beach Resort, Koh Mak

faq.q: Which beach is Ao Kao White Sand Beach Resort on, and what's nearby?
faq.a: The resort sits on Ao Kao Beach, at the eastern end, right next to Lazy Day The Resort. Ao Kao is a long beach on the southern side of Koh Mak, with white sand and coconut palms. The mid-beach restaurant cluster is about a 10-minute walk, and the Walking Street and Ao Suan Yai Beach are roughly a 5–10 minute drive.

faq.q: What does Ao Kao White Sand cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start at around ฿1,500/night for a garden-view villa in normal season. Pool and beachfront villas rise to roughly ฿2,200–3,600, and in peak season beachfront villas reach ฿5,000+. Every villa is brushed concrete, around 40 sqm, with a private roof terrace. Prices swing with the season, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is Ao Kao White Sand best for?
faq.a: It suits couples, groups of friends and families who want a modern beachfront villa. The standout is a private roof terrace on every villa, plus a seaview rooftop bar and warm service. It's not a luxury resort — it leans on contemporary design and a calm atmosphere at a price that's still reasonable.

faq.q: What's the beach like — can you swim there?
faq.a: The beach in front of the resort is fairly shallow at low tide with some rocky patches, so walking into deeper water isn't easy at every hour → check the tide chart before heading down, or use the resort pool when the tide is out. The sunsets on this side are lovely and the atmosphere is quiet.

faq.q: Is Koh Mak open year-round, and when should I go?
faq.a: The best window is high season, October–May, when the sea is clear and calm. In low season (Jun–mid-Oct) there's rain and swell, and many places on the island close → if you're going off-season, confirm with the resort that it's open and that boats are running before you book.
